trials.finding: Species identity and shared cartoon style are coherent; exact silhouette ratios still require measurement.
Airborne pose and identity are usable, but the requested transparent background was rendered as checkerboard pixels.
Text-only numeric ratios did not preserve the Mikado Pheasant's 230:100 tail-to-torso contract.
A conventional-style reference overrode the geometry guide and pulled the proportions off model.
Guide-only conditioning improved the long-tail silhouette substantially, but the visible tail-to-torso ratio remains outside the 6 percent acceptance tolerance.

The two-pass sheet contains exactly sixteen labeled, visibly airborne birds. A targeted Mikado edit substantially improved the diagnostic long-tail proportion; per-cell silhouette measurement remains required before production acceptance.

Seven long-tailed species were edited from v7 using parameter-derived cubic Bezier centerlines. Tail arc length is preserved while bend start, tip drop, tip tangent, and bundle coherence vary by species.

conclusion: Prompting is a candidate generator, not the geometry authority. Production characters need an approved component-separated anchor and deterministic rig/compositing for poses.
